note: Platform-as-a-service providers. Built-in means the platform provides it without a separate resource. Partner means the platform sells or integrates a service run by another company.

server: Fly Apps on always-on Fly Machines
Runs your containers as Firecracker-based Machines close to users, always on.
serverless: Fly Apps on auto-stopping Fly Machines
Runs your containers as Machines that stop when idle and start on the next request.

serverless.caveat: The first request after an idle period waits for a Machine to start.

any: Terminates TLS and load-balances requests to your Machines.
Routes users to the nearest region and absorbs basic traffic floods.

any.caveat: There is no separate web application firewall; add Cloudflare or a similar service in front if you need one.

any: A private IPv6 network between your apps that the internet cannot reach.
A managed PostgreSQL cluster with backups, run by Fly.io.
A managed Redis-compatible store sold through Fly.io.
S3-compatible object storage sold through Fly.io.
Encrypted values handed to your Machines as environment variables.
Stores the images Fly builds from your code.
Built-in metrics and logs, with an option to ship logs elsewhere.

any.caveat: Check current GPU availability and regions in the Fly.io documentation.

gaps.db_mysql: Run MySQL in a container on a Fly volume, or use a managed MySQL from a partner.
gaps.queue_kafka: Use Confluent Cloud or Redpanda Cloud.
gaps.search: Use a hosted search service such as Meilisearch Cloud or Elastic Cloud.
gaps.identity: Use a hosted sign-in service such as Clerk or Auth0.

any: Runs your app and workers as dynos, containers that Heroku builds and manages.

any.caveat: Dynos are always-on; there is no scale-to-zero. Router requests time out after 30 seconds, so stream or poll for long work.

any: Terminates TLS and routes requests to your dynos.
An isolated network for your dynos and data services.

any.caveat: Private Spaces are an Enterprise feature; smaller plans use shared infrastructure.

any: A managed PostgreSQL with backups and follower databases.
A managed Redis-compatible store used for caching and as a job queue broker.
Encrypted environment variables handed to your dynos.
Stores your container images when you deploy Docker images.
Collects your dyno logs and basic metrics, with log drains to other tools.

gaps.edge: Put Cloudflare or a similar CDN and firewall in front of the Heroku router.
gaps.search: Add a search add-on from the Heroku Elements marketplace.
gaps.storage: Use Amazon S3 or another object store; dynos have no persistent disk.
gaps.identity: Use a hosted sign-in service such as Auth0 or Clerk.
gaps.egress: Outbound traffic leaves the router's shared addresses; use a static-IP add-on if a partner requires a fixed address.

any: Runs your server-side code per request and scales automatically.

any.caveat: Netlify runs functions, not always-on containers. Each invocation has a time limit, so long jobs and persistent connections need another host.

any: Builds your front end and serves it from Netlify's CDN.
Terminates TLS and routes requests to your site and functions.
Serves cached content close to users and runs code at the edge.
Key-value and file storage for your site and functions.
A serverless PostgreSQL provisioned from Netlify and run by Neon.
Encrypted values handed to your builds and functions.
Netlify function logs and log drains
Shows function logs and can send them to other tools.

gaps.network: Netlify has no private network; keep data stores on a provider that restricts access by credentials and allow-lists.
gaps.db_mysql: Use PlanetScale or another managed MySQL.
gaps.queue_kafka: Use Confluent Cloud or Upstash Kafka.
gaps.registry: Not needed: Netlify builds from source.
gaps.identity: Use a hosted sign-in service such as Clerk or Auth0.

server: Builds and runs your containers, always on, with automatic deploys from your repository.
serverless: Runs your containers and puts them to sleep when idle.

serverless.caveat: A sleeping service takes a moment to wake on the next request.

any: Terminates TLS and routes requests to your services.
A private network between the services of a project.
A PostgreSQL database deployed from a Railway template.

any.caveat: It runs as a service in your project; set up backups and upgrades yourself.

any: A MySQL database deployed from a Railway template.

any.caveat: It runs as a service in your project; set up backups and upgrades yourself.

any: A MongoDB database deployed from a Railway template.

any.caveat: It runs as a service in your project; set up backups and upgrades yourself.

any: A Redis service deployed from a Railway template.

any.caveat: It runs as a service in your project; persistence and upgrades are yours to manage.

any: S3-compatible object storage inside a Railway project.
Encrypted values handed to your services as environment variables.
Shows service logs and resource metrics in the dashboard.

gaps.edge: Put Cloudflare or a similar CDN and firewall in front of the Railway proxy.
gaps.registry: Not needed: Railway builds from source or pulls public images.
gaps.identity: Use a hosted sign-in service such as Clerk or Auth0.
gaps.queue_kafka: Deploy Kafka from a template or use Confluent Cloud.

any: Render Web Services and Background Workers
Builds and runs your app and workers as containers with automatic deploys.

any.caveat: Free instances spin down when idle; paid instances stay on.

any: Builds your front end and serves it from Render's CDN.
Terminates TLS and routes requests to your services.
A private network between the services in a region.
A managed PostgreSQL with backups, run by Render.
A managed Redis-compatible store used for caching and as a job queue broker.
Render environment groups and secret files
Encrypted values handed to your services.
Shows service logs and metrics, with log streaming to other tools.

gaps.edge: Render includes a CDN for static sites; add Cloudflare in front for a firewall.
gaps.db_mysql: Run MySQL as a private service with a persistent disk, or use a managed MySQL from a partner.
gaps.storage: Render has no object storage; use Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2 or similar. Persistent disks are available for single-instance services.
gaps.registry: Not needed: Render builds from source or pulls images.
gaps.identity: Use a hosted sign-in service such as Clerk or Auth0.
gaps.queue_kafka: Use Confluent Cloud or Upstash Kafka.

any: Runs your server-side code per request and scales automatically.

any.caveat: Vercel runs functions, not always-on containers. Each invocation has a duration limit, so long jobs and persistent connections need another host.

any: Builds your front end and serves it from Vercel's global network.
Terminates TLS and routes requests to your site and functions.
Vercel Edge Network with Vercel Firewall
Serves cached content close to users and filters malicious traffic.
Neon Postgres through the Vercel Marketplace
A serverless PostgreSQL provisioned from Vercel and run by Neon.
MongoDB Atlas through the Vercel Marketplace
A managed MongoDB provisioned from Vercel and run by MongoDB.
Upstash Redis through the Vercel Marketplace
A managed Redis-compatible store provisioned from Vercel and run by Upstash.
Upstash Vector through the Vercel Marketplace
A managed vector index provisioned from Vercel and run by Upstash.
Object storage for files and uploads.
Encrypted values handed to your builds and functions.
Shows function logs and metrics and can send logs to other tools.

gaps.network: Vercel has no private network by default; restrict data stores by credentials and allow-lists, or use Secure Compute if your plan has it.
gaps.db_mysql: Use PlanetScale or another managed MySQL.
gaps.queue_kafka: Use Confluent Cloud or Upstash Kafka.
gaps.search: Use a hosted search service such as Algolia or Elastic Cloud.
gaps.registry: Not needed: Vercel builds from source.
gaps.identity: Use a hosted sign-in service such as Clerk or Auth0.
